messages:
morgan: FYI seeing a ~3x P95 latency spike starting ~11:07 UTC, correlated with a throughput drop on the inference pool. Alerts show a sudden jump in avg seq_len for requests.

alerts-bot: [ALERT] inference-pool-4 latency P95 1.2s -> 3.6s, error rate unchanged (0.2%) — triggered at 2026-03-18T11:07:47Z

zara: Noting that we had a customer demo hitting a lot of long tool-calls around then. Could be prompt-length distribution change. Starting profiling now.

kai: Quick check: kernel-selection logs show multiple fallbacks from optimized 8-bit kernel -> generic slower kernel for sequences > 8k tokens. That would explain latency per request jump.

morgan: Copy. I see a lot of KV cache growth in the runtime metrics (KV entries and memory per-session spiked). Possibly a tool-calling loop kept appending to context?

diego: Dumping a CPU profile and mem stats. Pushing pprof link: https://profiler.internal/pprof/1773824567/heap

kai: Pprof snapshot (trimmed):
```
# runtime/kvcache size by key-prefix
0.0MB  75%  kvcache/session/abc123/tool-output
12.8MB 20%  kvcache/session/abc412/long-prefix
2.4MB  5%   kvcache/session/xyz/other
# threadflame: kernel selection path heatmap shows hot fallback path at attention_kernel_generic
```

zara: Interesting — sessions with repeated tool outputs have huge prefix reuse but very long prefixes (~10k tokens) so prefix hashing bypasses prefix-caching heuristics and we end up storing large KV per request. That increases memory pressure and triggers smaller batch sizes because batcher sees high variance.

morgan: Reproduced locally with an integration test: a tiny fraction of clients that loop tool-call -> append result -> call again create long-running expanding contexts. End result: batching heuristic switches to conservative mode (max_batch = 8) and kernel selector chooses stable but slow kernels. Throughput down ~60%.

diego: Stack trace from slow kernel path:
```
#0 attention_generic_forward
#1 attention_blocking_dispatch
#2 kvcache::get_or_insert_slab
#3 runtime::serve_request
```

kai: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily cap per-session KV size (reject append if > X tokens) 2) tweak batcher to isolate high-variance sessions into their own nozzle so they don't shrink global batch size.

morgan: Rolling policy change: enforce transient per-session KV cap of 8192 tokens with 429 response and retry hint for now. Can we push to canary?

zara: Will implement policy in runtime config and push to canary pool-4. Also adding an automated alert when per-session KV > 6k to SRE.

sre-bot: Deploy queued: runtime-config-v2026-03-18-kvcap to canary (pool-4) — started 11:27 UTC

kai: Meanwhile we should add a fast path in kernel selector: prioritize small-batch optimized kernels for requests with very high seq_len variance instead of falling back to generic kernel. That way even if seq_len big, we keep throughput. I'll open an RFC.

diego: Added a short-term change to batcher: separate 'chatty' sessions (>=3 tool calls in 60s) into their own queue to avoid backpressure on short prompt bursts. Testing now.

morgan: Canary results: after kvcap + isolation, P95 dropped to 1.1s on canary, throughput recovered ~85%. Rolling to remainder of pool in 10m unless regressions.

zara: Follow-ups: 1) longer-term: add prefix-aware eviction to KV cache (evict repeated tool-output subprefixes), 2) kernel selector heuristic to avoid expensive generic kernels for common tool-loop patterns, 3) unit tests that simulate tool-loop growth.

morgan: Filed incident ticket INF-2026-03-18-01 with root cause notes and action items. Thanks all :bow:

kai: FYI I'm also adding telemetry to capture per-request kernel path and batch-size chosen so we can alert earlier next time.

zara: Leaving thread open for postmortem items. Good catch on combining kernel selection + KV behavior causing cascade.
